title: DLBCL Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL): workup and pathology -> disease state -> Ann Arbor stage / IPI risk / cell-of-origin and double-hit status / CNS risk -> stage- and biomarker-directed first-line arms -> response assessment -> relapsed / refractory pathway (CAR-T vs salvage + autologous transplant vs bispecific). Workup, staging, risk-stratification and surveillance content is standard oncology, not proprietary guideline text. The single leaf with a dose protocol references the existing R-CHOP Standard Protocol; arms without a dose protocol (pola-R-CHP, DA-EPOCH-R, CNS prophylaxis, CAR-T, salvage + ASCT, bispecifics) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated.

a.text: Risk in DLBCL is scored by the International Prognostic Index (IPI): one point each for age >60, stage III-IV, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, and >1 extranodal site. The NCCN-IPI refines age and LDH into graded bands. Higher score predicts lower cure rate and helps select treatment intensity.

b.text: For previously untreated patients with intermediate-to-high risk (IPI 2-5), substituting polatuzumab vedotin for vincristine (pola-R-CHP) improved progression-free survival versus R-CHOP in a randomized trial, with similar overall survival at first report.

c.text: CNS prophylaxis is considered for patients at high risk of central-nervous-system relapse (high CNS-IPI, or high-risk sites such as testis, breast, kidney/adrenal, paranasal sinus, or epidural). Options include high-dose intravenous methotrexate and/or intrathecal chemotherapy. Benefit is debated; the physician weighs risk against toxicity.

d.text: In primary-refractory disease or relapse within 12 months of first-line chemoimmunotherapy, second-line CD19 CAR T-cell therapy (axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel) improved event-free survival versus salvage chemotherapy plus autologous transplant in randomized trials. Late relapse (>=12 months) remains a candidate for salvage + autologous transplant.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation once DLBCL is suspected or confirmed. Establish histology, extent of disease, and fitness before therapy.

bullets.label: Excisional / core biopsy with expert hematopathology review
bullets.sub: confirm CD20-positive large B-cell histology; avoid relying on fine-needle aspirate alone

bullets.label: Immunohistochemistry and cell-of-origin
bullets.sub: CD20, CD10, BCL6, MUM1 (Hans algorithm: germinal-center vs non-germinal-center)

bullets.label: FISH for MYC, and if positive, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements
Contrast CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis and whole-body FDG-PET/CT for staging
Bone-marrow biopsy if PET is equivocal for marrow involvement
CBC, complete metabolic panel, LDH, uric acid; hepatitis B/C and HIV serology
Baseline echo / MUGA for ejection fraction before anthracycline
Assess CNS-relapse risk; lumbar puncture if high-risk features or neurologic signs
Fertility counseling; comorbidity and performance-status assessment

nodes.name: Disease state
nodes.title: Disease state
nodes.description: Choose the current clinical state. This drives whether to enter the newly-diagnosed staging pathway, the response-assessment pathway, or the relapsed / refractory pathway.

options.label: On / end of first-line therapy - response assessment
Relapsed or refractory after prior therapy

nodes.name: Pathology / biomarker
nodes.title: Pathology and biomarker subtype
nodes.description: Confirm the biology. Cell-of-origin and MYC / BCL2 / BCL6 rearrangement status separate ordinary DLBCL from high-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma and from transformed indolent lymphoma, which are treated differently.

tables.title: Cell-of-origin and rearrangement subtypes
rows: CD20+ large B-cells; Hans GCB vs non-GCB by IHC
Standard R-CHOP backbone; pola-R-CHP if IPI 2-5
MYC rearrangement plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement
Consider intensified DA-EPOCH-R; higher CNS risk
Large-cell transformation of prior low-grade lymphoma
Treat as DLBCL; prior therapy affects options

nodes.name: Ann Arbor stage
nodes.title: Staging and disease extent
nodes.description: Assign Ann Arbor stage from PET/CT. Limited (non-bulky I-II) and advanced (III-IV, or bulky II) disease follow different first-line pathways.

tables.title: Ann Arbor stage (Lugano modification)
rows: One node region or one extranodal site
Two or more node regions on the same side of the diaphragm
Node regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Diffuse extranodal involvement (e.g. marrow, liver, lung)
Bulky mass (commonly >=7.5 cm) or B symptoms modify risk

nodes.name: Limited risk
nodes.title: Limited-stage: risk features
nodes.description: Within limited stage, the presence of bulk or adverse risk factors (elevated LDH, age >60, ECOG >=2, stage II) determines whether an abbreviated PET-guided course or a full six-cycle course is used.

nodes.name: Interim PET
nodes.title: Favorable limited: PET-guided abbreviation
nodes.description: For favorable non-bulky disease an interim FDG-PET after a few cycles guides whether a shortened course (chemoimmunotherapy plus involved-site radiation, or a slightly longer chemo-only course) is sufficient.

nodes.name: Abbreviated R-CHOP
nodes.title: Favorable limited, PET-negative: abbreviated R-CHOP
nodes.description: PET-negative favorable limited-stage disease can be cured with a shortened course.
bullets: R-CHOP x 3 cycles followed by involved-site radiation, OR R-CHOP x 4-6 cycles with no radiation
Confirm end-of-treatment PET (Deauville 1-3) documents complete metabolic response
The dose engine computes the R-CHOP regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Extended R-CHOP + RT
nodes.title: Favorable limited, PET-positive: extend R-CHOP + radiation
nodes.description: A positive interim PET calls for a full course and, usually, consolidative radiation to residual disease.
bullets: Complete R-CHOP to 6 cycles and add involved-site radiation to the PET-positive site
Biopsy a persistently PET-positive residual mass to exclude refractory disease
R-CHOP regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Full R-CHOP +/- RT
nodes.title: Unfavorable limited: full R-CHOP +/- radiation
nodes.description: Bulky or adverse-factor limited disease is treated like advanced disease with a full course, with radiation to bulk.
bullets: R-CHOP x 6 cycles
Consolidative radiation to sites of bulky disease
Consider CNS-risk assessment as for advanced disease
R-CHOP regimen referenced below

nodes.name: CNS risk
nodes.title: Advanced: CNS-relapse risk
nodes.description: Before or alongside systemic therapy, stratify CNS-relapse risk (CNS-IPI plus high-risk anatomic sites) to decide on prophylaxis.

tables.title: CNS-IPI risk factors
rows: Age >60, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, stage III-IV, >1 extranodal site
Testis, breast, epidural, paranasal sinus, uterus - consider prophylaxis regardless of score

nodes.name: CNS prophylaxis
nodes.title: High CNS risk: prophylaxis plus systemic therapy
nodes.description: Add CNS-directed prophylaxis to standard systemic chemoimmunotherapy.
bullets: High-dose intravenous methotrexate and/or intrathecal chemotherapy alongside the systemic regimen
Then treat the systemic disease with the appropriate IPI-directed arm (R-CHOP or pola-R-CHP), or DA-EPOCH-R for double-hit disease
Benefit of prophylaxis is uncertain - individualize against renal function and toxicity
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Fitness
nodes.title: Advanced: fitness for full-dose therapy
nodes.description: Physiologic fitness and cardiac reserve determine whether full-dose anthracycline-based therapy or an attenuated regimen is appropriate.

nodes.name: Attenuated therapy
nodes.title: Frail / elderly: attenuated R-CHOP
nodes.description: For patients unfit for full-dose therapy, a reduced-intensity regimen preserves curative intent while limiting toxicity.
bullets: R-mini-CHOP (attenuated doses) for patients over about 80 or with limited reserve
Pre-phase steroids and careful cardiac monitoring; consider liposomal anthracycline or non-anthracycline backbone if EF is low
Growth-factor support and infection prophylaxis
R-CHOP-class regimen referenced below; the dose engine applies attenuation

nodes.name: Advanced biology
nodes.title: Advanced (fit): double-hit vs standard
nodes.description: High-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma may warrant an intensified regimen; otherwise proceed to IPI-directed selection.

nodes.name: DA-EPOCH-R
nodes.title: Double-hit: intensified DA-EPOCH-R
nodes.description: High-grade double- / triple-hit lymphoma is often treated with a dose-adjusted infusional regimen with CNS prophylaxis.
bullets: Dose-adjusted EPOCH-R (rituximab, etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin) with dose escalation by nadir counts
Include CNS prophylaxis given the higher CNS-relapse risk
Reassess with end-of-treatment PET; enroll in a trial where available
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: IPI selection
nodes.title: Advanced (fit, standard): IPI-directed backbone
nodes.description: IPI risk selects between the R-CHOP backbone and the polatuzumab-containing pola-R-CHP backbone.

nodes.name: R-CHOP
nodes.title: Advanced, IPI 0-1: R-CHOP x 6
nodes.description: Six cycles of R-CHOP is the standard backbone for low-risk advanced DLBCL.
bullets: R-CHOP x 6 cycles (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone)
Interim and end-of-treatment PET to confirm response
Growth-factor support and tumor-lysis prophylaxis for high burden
R-CHOP regimen referenced below

nodes.name: pola-R-CHP
nodes.title: Advanced, IPI 2-5: pola-R-CHP
nodes.description: For intermediate-to-high-risk disease, polatuzumab vedotin replaces vincristine (pola-R-CHP), which improved progression-free survival versus R-CHOP.
bullets: Pola-R-CHP x 6 cycles: polatuzumab vedotin + rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone (vincristine omitted)
Followed by 2 further doses of rituximab
Monitor for peripheral neuropathy and cytopenias
R-CHOP remains an acceptable alternative; no pola-R-CHP dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Response
nodes.title: End-of-treatment response assessment
nodes.description: Restage with FDG-PET at the end of first-line therapy. A complete metabolic response moves to surveillance; residual disease enters the relapsed / refractory pathway.

nodes.name: Relapse workup
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: confirm and restage
nodes.description: Confirm relapse histologically and restage before choosing a second-line strategy.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm relapse and exclude a different histology or transformation
PET/CT restaging; re-check LDH, organ function, hepatitis/HIV status
Assess fitness, prior anthracycline exposure, and candidacy for cellular therapy
Re-evaluate CNS risk and symptoms

nodes.name: Cellular-therapy fit
nodes.title: Relapsed: fit for intensive / cellular therapy?
nodes.description: Candidacy for CAR T-cell therapy or high-dose therapy with autologous transplant separates the intensive pathway from the non-intensive pathway.

nodes.name: Relapse timing
nodes.title: Fit relapse: timing / prior cellular therapy
nodes.description: Timing of relapse relative to first-line therapy, and whether the patient has already had cellular therapy or transplant, selects the second-line strategy.

options.label: Progression after prior CAR-T or transplant

nodes.name: CAR T-cell
nodes.title: Early / refractory relapse: second-line CD19 CAR-T
nodes.description: For primary-refractory disease or relapse within 12 months, second-line CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is preferred over salvage plus transplant.
bullets: Axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel (CD19 CAR-T)
Bridging therapy may be needed while cells are manufactured
Monitor for cytokine-release syndrome and neurotoxicity (ICANS); manage at a certified center
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Salvage + ASCT
nodes.title: Late relapse: salvage chemo then autologous transplant
nodes.description: For relapse at or beyond 12 months in a transplant-fit patient, platinum-based salvage followed by high-dose therapy and autologous stem-cell transplant remains standard.
bullets: Platinum-based salvage chemoimmunotherapy (e.g. R-ICE, R-DHAP, R-GDP)
If chemosensitive: high-dose conditioning (e.g. BEAM) and autologous stem-cell transplant
If chemorefractory: proceed to CD19 CAR T-cell therapy
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Non-intensive line
nodes.title: Not transplant / CAR-T eligible: line of therapy
nodes.description: For patients who are not cellular-therapy candidates, the number of prior lines guides selection among antibody-drug conjugates, immunomodulatory combinations, and bispecific antibodies.

nodes.name: Pola-BR / Tafa-len
nodes.title: Second line, non-transplant: pola-BR or tafasitamab-lenalidomide
nodes.description: Transplant-ineligible second-line options combine targeted agents with chemotherapy or immunomodulation.
bullets: Polatuzumab vedotin + bendamustine + rituximab (pola-BR)
Or tafasitamab + lenalidomide for transplant-ineligible patients
Or rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) for less-fit patients
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Bispecific antibody
nodes.title: Third line or beyond: CD20xCD3 bispecific
nodes.description: In the third-line-and-beyond setting, off-the-shelf CD20xCD3 bispecific antibodies provide durable responses.
bullets: Glofitamab (fixed-duration) or epcoritamab (continuous) CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody
Step-up dosing with CRS monitoring and tumor-lysis precautions
Loncastuximab tesirine is an alternative single agent
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Post-cellular relapse
nodes.title: Progression after CAR-T / transplant: next options
nodes.description: After prior cellular therapy or transplant, options are non-cross-resistant agents, bispecifics, allogeneic transplant in selected fit patients, or a clinical trial.
bullets: CD20xCD3 bispecific antibody (glofitamab or epcoritamab) if not already used
Loncastuximab tesirine, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, or pola-BR depending on prior exposure
Consider allogeneic transplant in selected younger, fit, chemosensitive patients
Prioritize clinical-trial enrollment
No dose protocol here - shown as guidance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Follow-up after a complete response. Most relapses occur within the first 2 years; routine surveillance imaging is limited.
bullets: History, exam, and labs (CBC, LDH) every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months to 5 years
Routine surveillance CT/PET is not recommended in asymptomatic remission; image for symptoms or exam findings
Educate on relapse symptoms; biopsy any suspected relapse before treating
Monitor for late effects: cardiac (anthracycline), second malignancy, and infection risk
